Johnson High School|J.O. Johnson]]
(Huntsville, Alabama) * [[Jemison High School (Huntsville)|Jemison]] (Huntsville, Alabama) | college = [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] (2017–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | career_start = 2021 | years1 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021]]–[[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]] | team1 = [[Birmingham Squadron]] | highlights = * First-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] – Coaches (2021) * Second-team All-SEC – [[Associated Press|AP]] (2021) * Second-team All-SEC – Coaches (2020) * 2× [[Alabama Mr. Basketball]] (2016, 2017) }} '''John Petty Jr.''' (born December 2, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama Crimson Tide]]. ==High school career== As a freshman at [[J.O. Johnson High School]] in [[Huntsville, Alabama]], Petty led his team to the state championship game and earned first-team Class 4A All-State honors.{{cite web |last1=Boyette |first1=Daniel |title=J.O. Johnson's John Petty, one of nation's most touted sophomores, takes attention in stride |url=https://www.al.com/highschoolsports/article/jo-johnsons-john-petty-one-of-natons-most-touted-sophomores-takes-attention-in-stride/ |website=[[AL.com]] |accessdate=February 28, 2020 |date=January 29, 2015}} In his sophomore season, he won the Class 5A state title and was named tournament [[most valuable player]] (MVP). He was named Class 5A player of the year and finished third in [[Alabama Mr. Basketball]] voting.{{cite web |title=J.O. Johnson boys win 5A state championship |url=https://www.wbrc.com/story/28229492/jo-johnson-boys-win-5a-state-championship/ |website=[[WBRC]] |accessdate=February 28, 2020 |date=March 1, 2015}} As a junior, Petty averaged 19.9 points, 7.1 rebounds and 4.1 assists per game, shooting 51 percent from the field and leading J.O. Johnson to its second straight Class 5A state championship. He repeated as tournament MVP after scoring 34 points in the title game and was recognized as Alabama Mr. Basketball and Alabama [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]].{{cite web |last1=Boyette |first1=Daniel |title=J.O. Johnson's John Petty named Gatorade Alabama Boys Basketball Player of the Year |url=https://www.al.com/highschoolsports/article/jo-johnsons-john-petty-named-gatorade-alabama-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year/ |website=[[AL.com]] |accessdate=February 28, 2020 |date=March 17, 2016}}{{cite web |last1=Boyette |first1=Daniel |title=J.O. Johnson's John Petty named Mr. Basketball after stellar season |url=https://www.al.com/highschoolsports/article/jo-johnsons-john-petty-named-mr-basketball-after-stellar-season/ |website=[[AL.com]] |accessdate=February 28, 2020 |date=April 6, 2016}} For his senior season, Petty moved to [[Jemison High School (Huntsville)|Jemison High School]] after the closure of J.O Johnson. He averaged 20.7 points, 7.7 rebounds and 5.6 assists per game, won his third consecutive Class 5A state title and became the third player to win Alabama Mr. Basketball twice.{{cite web |last1=Long |first1=A. Stacy |title=Petty again Mr. Basketball |url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/high-school/2017/04/04/petty-again-mr-basketball-beats-2-fellow-tide-signees/100036982/ |website=[[Montgomery Advertiser]] |accessdate=February 28, 2020 |date=April 4, 2017}}{{cite web |last1=Boyette |first1=Daniel |title=John Petty leads Mae Jemison past Faith Academy for Class 5A boys title |url=https://www.al.com/highschoolsports/article/john-petty-leads-mae-jemison-past-faith-academy-for-class-5a-boys-title/ |website=[[AL.com]] |accessdate=February 28, 2020 |date=March 4, 2017}} He was selected to play at the [[Jordan Brand Classic]].{{cite web |last1=Smith |first1=Cam |title=John Petty is pumped about Jordan Brand Classic honor |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/john-petty-is-pumped-about-jordan-brand-classic-honor |website=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=February 28, 2020 |date=February 6, 2017}} ===Recruiting=== A five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[ESPN]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] the top player from Alabama in the 2017 class, Petty committed to play college basketball for [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] over [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]].{{cite web |last1=Roberts |first1=Ben |title=2017 basketball recruit John Petty picks Alabama, so where does UK look next? |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article114060773.html |website=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |accessdate=February 28, 2020 |date=November 10, 2016}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2017}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = John Petty Jr. | position = [[Shooting guard|SG]] | hometown = [[Huntsville, Alabama|Huntsville, AL]] | highschool = [[Jemison High School (Huntsville)|Jemison]] (AL) | feet = 6 | inches = 5 | weight = 185 | 40 = | commitdate = November 10, 2016 | scout stars = 4 | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 93 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2017 | rivals ref title = Alabama 2017 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2017 Alabama Crimson Tide Recruiting Class | rivals school = alabama | scout s = | espn schoolid = 333 | scout overall = 46 | rivals overall = 28 | 247 overall = 34 | espn overall = 22 | accessdate = February 28, 2020 | bball = yes }} ==College career== [[File:John Petty.jpg|thumb|upright|Petty in 2019]] On November 17, 2017, in his third collegiate game, Petty scored a season-high 30 points and made a school-record 10 three-pointers in a 104–67 win over [[Alabama A&M Bulldogs basketball|Alabama A&M]].{{cite web |last1=Wittry |first1=Andy |title=Alabama's John Petty catches fire for 10 3s against Alabama A&M |url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2017-11-17/college-basketball-alabamas-john-petty-makes-school-record-10 |publisher=[[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] |accessdate=March 5, 2020 |date=November 17, 2017}} It was the most efficient three-point shooting performance by a player who recorded at least 10 three-pointers in [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) history. Petty was subsequently named SEC Freshman of the Week.{{cite web |last1=Potter |first1=Charlie |title=Alabama's John Petty named SEC Freshman of the Week |url=https://247sports.com/college/alabama/Article/Alabama-Crimson-Tide-Basketball-John-Petty-named-SEC-Freshman-of-the-Week-110805663/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=March 5, 2020 |date=November 20, 2017}} He won the award again on January 1, 2018, two days after posting 18 points, four rebounds and three assists in a 79–57 victory over fifth-ranked [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]].{{cite web |last1=Zenor |first1=John |title=John Petty, Alabama topple No. 5 Texas A&M 79-57 |url=https://apnews.com/e457c88beaa34db5b71aeb18de01771e |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=March 5, 2020 |date=December 30, 2017}} As a freshman, Petty averaged 10.2 points, 2.6 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game for the Crimson Tide.{{cite web |last1=Byington |first1=Alex |title=Alabama basketball's John Petty Jr. finds balance in basketball, parenthood |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/sec/2019/12/07/alabama-basketball-john-petty-basketball-parenthood/4364810002/ |website=[[USA Today]] |accessdate=February 28, 2020 |date=December 7, 2019}} On January 19, 2019, in his sophomore season, Petty matched his career high of 30 points in a 71–68 loss to third-ranked [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]].{{cite web |last1=Byington |first1=Alex |title=3 takeaways from Alabama's 71-68 loss at No. 3 Tennessee |url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/2019/01/19/second-half-barrage-alabamas-petty-not-enough-vs-no-3-ut/2626963002/ |website=[[Montgomery Advertiser]] |accessdate=March 5, 2020 |date=January 19, 2019}} As a sophomore, he averaged 10.2 points, 4.2 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game. After the season, he entered the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) transfer portal.{{cite web |last1=Zenitz |first1=Matt |title=John Petty plans to stay at Alabama instead of transferring |url=https://www.al.com/alabamabasketball/2019/03/john-petty-plans-to-stay-at-alabama-instead-of-transferring.html |website=[[AL.com]] |accessdate=March 5, 2020 |date=March 29, 2019}} After having a meeting with new coach [[Nate Oats]], Petty removed his name from the transfer portal on April 2. On November 28, 2019, Petty recorded a then-career-high 34 points and 12 rebounds, his first career [[double (basketball)|double-double]], in a 104–89 loss to [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]] at the [[Battle 4 Atlantis]].{{cite web |title=John Petty Jr.'s Career Night Not Enough for Alabama to Overtake Iowa State at Battle 4 Atlantis Tournament |url=https://rolltide.com/news/2019/11/28/mens-basketball-isu.aspx |publisher=University of Alabama Athletics |accessdate=March 5, 2020 |date=November 28, 2019}} He established a new career high on December 18, scoring 39 points in a 105–87 win over [[Samford Bulldogs men's basketball|Samford]]. He had 10 three-pointers in the game, tying his own school record.{{cite web |last1=Rodak |first1=Mike |title=Alabama's John Petty scores 39 points in historic win over Samford |url=https://www.al.com/alabamabasketball/2019/12/alabamas-john-petty-scores-39-points-in-historic-win-over-samford.html |website=[[AL.com]] |accessdate=March 5, 2020 |date=December 18, 2019}} Five days later, Petty shared SEC Player of the Week honors with Jair Bolden of [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]].{{cite magazine |title=Alabama's John Petty Jr. Named Co-SEC Men's Basketball Player of the Week |url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/bamacentral/alabamas-john-petty-jr-named-co-sec-mens-basketball-player-of-the-week |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |accessdate=March 5, 2020 |date=December 23, 2019}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Petty was named to the Second Team All-SEC.{{cite press release|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/28877731/sec-announces-2020-men-basketball-awards |title=SEC announces 2020 Men's Basketball Awards |publisher=Southeastern Conference |date=March 10, 2020 |accessdate=March 10, 2020}} As a junior, Petty averaged 14.5 points, 6.6 rebounds, and 2.5 assists per game.{{cite web |last1=Tsoukalas |first1=Tony |title=How to watch: Alabama basketball vs Tennessee in the SEC Tournament |url=https://alabama.rivals.com/news/how-to-watch-alabama-basketball-vs-tennessee-in-the-sec-tournament |website=Rivals.com |date=11 March 2020 |accessdate=March 22, 2020}} After the season, Petty declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite web |last1=Potter |first1=Charlie |title=Alabama's Kira Lewis, John Petty to test NBA draft waters |url=https://247sports.com/college/alabama/Article/Alabama-Basketball-Kira-Lewis-John-Petty-to-test-NBA-draft-waters-145346895/ |website=247 Sports |date=March 24, 2020|accessdate=March 25, 2020}} However, on August 3, he announced he was withdrawing from the draft and returning to Alabama.{{cite news |last1=Edwards |first1=Mark |title=Alabama basketball: John Petty to stay |url=https://www.newspressnow.com/sports/college/alabama-basketball-john-petty-to-stay/article_afb818e9-e2e0-5cf3-b5e5-b2486260674b.html |accessdate=August 4, 2020 |work=[[St. Joseph News-Press]] |date=August 3, 2020 }}{{Dead link|date=November 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} On January 16, 2021, Petty became the all-time three-point scoring leader for Alabama in a 90–59 win against [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]], finishing with 17 points.{{cite news |title=Alabama routs Arkansas 90-59 |url=https://katv.com/sports/hog-central/alabama-routs-arkansas-90-59 |access-date=October 14, 2021 |work=KATV |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 16, 2021}} As a senior, he averaged 12.6 points, 5.2 rebounds, and 1.9 assists per game, and hit an SEC-leading 77 three-pointers. Petty was named to the First Team All-SEC.{{cite magazine |last1=Blackwell |first1=Joey |title=John Petty Jr. Signs with New Orleans Pelicans |url=https://www.si.com/college/alabama/bamacentral/john-petty-jr-signs-with-new-orleans-pelicans-blackwell |access-date=October 14, 2021 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=October 13, 2021}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Petty signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] on October 14, 2021.{{cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans sign John Petty Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/new-orleans-pelicans-sign-guard-john-petty-jr|website=NBA.com|date=October 14, 2021|access-date=November 2, 2021}} However, he was waived two days later.{{cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans waive guard John Petty Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/new-orleans-pelicans-waive-guard-john-petty-jr|website=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2021|access-date=November 2, 2021}} On October 25, he signed with the [[Birmingham Squadron]] as an affiliate player.{{cite web|title=Birmingham Squadron finalize roster for team's first training camp in Birmingham|url=https://birmingham.gleague.nba.com/news/birmingham-squadron-announce-2021-training-camp-roster/|work=NBA.com|date=October 25, 2021|access-date=November 2, 2021}} Petty spent two seasons with the Squadron and averaged 7.3 points, 3.4 rebounds and 1.8 assists in 89 games.{{cite web |last1=Inabinett |first1=Mark |title=Former Alabama standout leaves Birmingham in NBA G League trade |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2023/09/former-alabama-standout-leaves-birmingham-in-nba-g-league-trade.html |website=AL |access-date=June 14, 2024 |date=September 8, 2023}} On September 8, 2023, Petty's mother is Regina and he has two sisters. He has a daughter, Aubrielle Nicole Petty, who was born during his freshman season in college. The mother of Aubrielle is Tamarra Fletcher, who also played basketball at Jemison High.
